originality.rationale: The Gabor ambiguity-diagonalization formula itself is established by Bojarovska–Flinth (Theorem 2.3) and is not claimed new. The statement requiring comparison is instead the global minimax over every complex impulse parameter in the prime one-spike family, uniquely achieved at imaginary spikes. Positive-real-spike results cover only a proper subfamily with asymptotically twice the condition number; no assessed published primary theorem yields the present complex-phase optimum. Residual risk: equivalent earlier one-spike design work might exist.
residual_risks: A prior algebraic signal-design article might have derived the same one-impulse complex-phase optimum under alternate terminology; bounded searches cannot eliminate that possibility.
The 2026 general-window work was abstract-inspected only; it is not a decisive unresolved competing statement for the sharply restricted window class.
Stability is Hilbert–Schmidt lifted conditioning, not the nonlinear signal-distance phase-retrieval Lipschitz constant.

value.rationale: Two-level flat-plus-single-spike generators are a natural minimal-complexity phase-retrievable window design. The result gives the precise best possible singular margin across all complex spike amplitudes, all equality parameters, an unavoidable p^(3/2) conditioning growth, and the phase-induced asymptotic factor-two improvement over positive-real spikes. This is a structurally motivated complete design classification; no claim is made of global optimality among all windows.
